## My Reasoning

My family has farmed this same land for three generations. In Quzhou, everyone grows winter wheat then summer maize — that's just what you do here. The soil is good for it, the water is there underground, and the buyers at the grain station take everything. I don't know why I'd try anything else. My father did it, I do it, that's the way.

I have 9 mu total. I'll plant all of it to wheat this October, then flip it to maize right after the June harvest. Same land, two crops a year — that's normal here.

For wheat, I'll buy Jimai 22 seed from the township supply cooperative. Everyone I know uses it. I'll spread diammonium phosphate and potash before I till, then broadcast urea again at jointing in March. I water before sowing to get germination going, then again at jointing, and again at heading — three times is what I've always done. I spray a herbicide in early spring and watch for rust and powdery mildew — if I see it, I spray again.

For maize I use Xianyu 335 — the hybrid bags. Same as my neighbors. Summer rain usually handles most of the water but if July is dry I'll pump once at tasseling. I put compound fertilizer in at planting then top-dress urea when it's knee-high. Maybe spray once for armyworm if it shows up.

I'm not trying anything new this year. Prices were okay last year and I don't want to risk my family's income experimenting.
